_readme: Source for the game notes' two generated sections (build_bits.py renders them on bits/wax-baseball/ between the ROSTER and ERRORS markers). roster: one card-back per tool, in this order; name/position/url/what/did are hand-authored copy; tags are the tool names as they appear in pieces.json `tools`, and the generator matches them to compute 'Bats in' (the lineup) and 'Also played' (the away games), so that line is never typed. errors: every wrong answer in the run; `slug` is the piece it bats in, and the generator renders the link with that piece's current slot label. Every number here comes from the receipts sheet (wax-system: wax-baseball/narration/99-receipts.md) or the piece's own page.

errors.kind: Instruction. Skipped the step it was told it must take.
Grounding. Invented, no tool call. Still open.
Context. Decided “I” meant the logged-in user.
Path. The join never ran through my games.
Path. Batters only; pitchers never entered.
Load. Kept one Hall of Fame ballot per player.
Validation. The agent path rejected column names the SQL path accepted.

roster.name: dbt on BigQuery
roster.what: SQL that runs inside the warehouse and turns raw tables into tested, documented ones. Its semantic layer is where each metric gets written once.
roster.did: 16 models, 104 tests green, 7 governed metrics. Every other engine is measured against it.

roster.name: BigQuery
roster.what: Google's warehouse. Where the 178 games and their 14,406 plays live, and where the whole thing started as a spreadsheet upload.
roster.did: Its own agent narrated in plain English and handed over a job id you can look up. 9.5 seconds, 0 bytes billed.

roster.name: Tableau Cloud
roster.what: Classic Tableau, hosted. You know it. This time an agent wrote the workbook as XML and published it through the Tableau MCP server.
roster.did: 34 bars, 400 home runs, no browser open. 7 for 7 through the query service.

roster.name: Tableau Next
roster.what: Tableau on Salesforce's platform. It reads the Data 360 semantic model directly, and Tableau Agent answers questions over it.
roster.did: First answer: zero home runs, confidently. After the model learned who “I” is: 4 for 4.

roster.name: Data 360
roster.what: Salesforce's data layer. It reads Snowflake and Databricks where they sit, copies from Google Cloud, and holds the semantic model Salesforce's agents stand on.
roster.did: 7 for 7 through the semantic engine. Said 281 Hall of Famers before it said 44.

roster.name: Agentforce
roster.what: Salesforce's agent platform. Baseball Scout is written in Agent Script: the agent as code, not clicks.
roster.did: 3 golden cases, 3 for 3, three runs straight. Also committed the 9 and the 0%.

roster.name: Snowflake
roster.what: A cloud warehouse. The seven metrics live in a semantic view, and Cortex is the agent that answers from it.
roster.did: 7 for 7. The agent got to 400 by rewriting the home run definition by hand instead of asking for it by name.

roster.name: Databricks
roster.what: A lakehouse. The metrics live in Unity Catalog metric views. Genie is its agent, AI/BI draws its charts.
roster.did: 7 for 7. Genie asked for the measure by name, then volunteered its own assumption.

roster.name: Claude
roster.what: Anthropic's agent SDK. This agent has no SQL tool. The only thing it can do with your data is ask for a metric by name.
roster.did: 4 tool calls to the right answer. A twin with raw SQL needed 9. $0.18 for the turn.

roster.name: Streamlit
roster.what: Python apps that live inside Snowflake. The chart reads the same semantic view the agent does.
roster.did: The same 400 by year, deployed from the command line.

roster.name: Looker Studio
roster.what: Google's free BI tool, reading the same BigQuery view.
roster.did: The one chart drawn by hand. No authoring API, and the page says so.
